recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not re-add DSM-5 as a core External Code Systems row; if DSM-5 implementer guidance is still needed, pursue it through HTA/THO and reflect that DSM-5 uses ICD code systems rather than native DSM-5 codes.
issue_request: FHIR-13998 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 Vocabulary request to add DSM-5 as a terminology system, creating http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/dsm5 and OID 2.16.840.1.113883.6.344.
initial_application: The request was applied by git commit c4bc403b9ba207d349b54115fa9dcf13f33732d5, svn revision 13081, which added a DSM-5 row with the requested URI and OID to source/terminologies-systems.html.
additional_context: HTA-8 and the 2021-12-16 HTA minutes later concluded DSM-5 is not a standalone code system with native codes, while acknowledging the already-published R4 URI could not simply be removed from that release. FHIR-37853 was then Published/Persuasive for R5 and moved authoritative external terminology and identifier information out of FHIR core and into THO, deleting core External Code Systems rows without Using-X-with-FHIR pages, including DSM-5.
reconciliation: No core source was changed. Current source/terminologies-systems.html already says core is authoritative for FHIR-defined code systems, external terminology content in the Defined Externally tab is non-authoritative, and THO is authoritative for external terminology URI/OID information. Re-adding DSM-5 to core would conflict with FHIR-37853 and HTA-8.
